title: Affine formal modules: reconstruction assembly
statement: Objectwise reconstruction isomorphisms satisfying the projection naturality assemble to a natural isomorphism.

proof.text: For each F and level n, transpose the given sections projection through the affine tilde/Gamma adjunction. Naturality of ideal products and annihilation of the target level imply that this transpose kills the ideal-power product, so cokernel.desc defines a sheaf quotient comparison q with its projection equation.

The adjunction unit naturality and right triangle identify the sections of the transpose after the unit with the given surjective projection. Therefore Gamma(q) is epi. The assumed objectwise isomorphism supplies a separate levelwise isomorphism i. The coherent target has finite affine sections; restriction along the global-sections ring isomorphism makes them finite over A. The composite i.inv followed by Gamma(q) is a surjective endomorphism of that finite module, hence bijective. Consequently Gamma(q) is an isomorphism. Counit naturality with i makes the source counit invertible, and counit naturality with q then makes q invertible.

Choose the now uniquely determined quotient comparisons. For each transition precompose both sides with the source cokernel projection, use cokernel.pi_desc and the projection equation, then use naturality of p and the counit. Cancel the epi projection and assemble the inverse-system isomorphism with NatIso.ofComponents; lift it to the full coherent-formal subcategory.

For a morphism F to G, precompose each level of the outer naturality equation with the quotient projection. The quotient-map equation and the projection equations reduce this to hnatural, mapped by tilde and composed with the counit. Cancel the projection; componentwise equality and NatIso.ofComponents give the stated natural isomorphism.
